user.title: mpubsub
user.description: Brokerless IPv6-multicast pub/sub. Home Assistant must be able to send and receive IPv6 multicast on the same network segment as your devices — a container on the default bridge network cannot, and will silently receive nothing.

data_description.port: Must match the `port:` on your devices.
data_description.scope: Must match the `scope:` on your devices. A different scope is a different multicast group, so a mismatch means silence rather than an error.
data_description.interface: Leave blank to let the kernel choose. Required in practice on a host with more than one network interface, since only one link is joined.
data_description.encryption_key: The same passphrase as your devices' `encryption: key:`. Leave blank for plaintext.

error.cannot_connect: Could not open the multicast socket: {error}. Check that the port is free and that this host has IPv6 enabled.
error.unknown_interface: No such network interface on this host.

error.replay_window_needs_key: A replay window needs an encryption passphrase: replay protection only ever applies to encrypted packets.
error.indefinite_needs_delay: An indefinite retransmit count (-1) needs a retransmit delay of at least 1 second, or it will saturate the network.
error.invalid_retransmit_count: Retransmit count must be 1 to 255, or -1 for indefinite. Every publish sends at least one datagram, so 0 is meaningless.

data_description.hops: IPv6 multicast hop limit. 1 keeps traffic on the local segment.
data_description.retransmit_count: Datagrams sent per publish. 1 disables retransmission; -1 keeps resending until another publish to the same topic supersedes it. Without encryption and a replay window, each retransmit is delivered again.
data_description.promote_qos: Map the qos argument of mpubsub.publish onto the retransmit count: 0 leaves it alone, 1 raises it to at least 3, 2 resends until superseded. Never a delivery guarantee — nothing acknowledges anything.
data_description.replay_window: Seconds of clock skew to accept on encrypted packets, and how long to remember nonces for de-duplication. 0 disables replay protection. Only ever applies to encrypted traffic.

publish.name: Publish
publish.description: Publishes a message to an mpubsub topic.

topic.name: Topic
topic.description: Topic to publish to. Wildcards (+ and #) are not supported.

payload.name: Payload
payload.description: Payload to publish. Up to ~1220 bytes, less when encrypted.

evaluate_payload.name: Evaluate payload
evaluate_payload.description: Evaluate the payload as a Python literal, so a bytes literal such as b'\x01' can be sent.

qos.name: QoS
qos.description: Only has an effect when the Promote QoS option is on, where it raises the retransmit count. Not a delivery guarantee.

retain.name: Retain
retain.description: Accepted for compatibility with MQTT-shaped code and ignored: mpubsub has no retain flag and no broker to store messages.

listen.name: Listen
listen.description: Subscribes to a topic for a while and reports what arrives. The replacement for the MQTT panel's 'Listen to a topic'. Messages are returned in the response and fired on the event bus as mpubsub_message_received, watchable in Developer Tools > Events.

topic.name: Topic
topic.description: Exact topic to listen to. Wildcards are not supported, so there is no way to dump all traffic.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How many seconds to listen before unsubscribing.

encoding.name: Encoding
encoding.description: Text codec used to decode payloads. Leave blank to report raw bytes as hex.
